harmonicFunction: Am (i) - Heavy, moody minor tonic establishing intense emotional urgency
G (♭VII) - Mixolydian subtonic creating forward rock momentum and vocal release
F (♭VI) - Dramatic submediant chord delivering maximum emotional tension in the Aeolian cadence
E7 (V7) - Harmonic minor dominant providing classical leading-tone resolution in the acoustic intro

techniques.name: Flamenco-Style Acoustic Pull-Offs & High-Speed Strumming
techniques.description: Executing Nancy Wilson's virtuosic acoustic introduction featuring lightning-fast pull-offs on the B and G strings, rapid strumming rasgueado accents, and seamless transitions into electric power chords

notes: Silver Wheels pull-off flurry: Rapid sixteenth notes pulling off from C (fret 1 B) to open B and open G
Acoustic attack: Nancy Wilson uses a flatpick combined with fingers (hybrid picking) on an acoustic dreadnought
Electric bridge transition: Heavy downstroke palm muting on the low E string locking with the kick drum at 130 BPM
sequence: Master the finger agility for the open B string pull-off pattern at 90 BPM
Build metronome speed on the acoustic prelude up to performance tempo of 130 BPM
Practice the dramatic sudden switch from acoustic fingerstyle to aggressive electric chugging
Execute the full Aeolian power chord cadence (Am - G - F - G) with tight rhythmic punch
tips: Use a heavy gauge acoustic pick (0.88mm to 1.0mm) to get a loud, crisp, cutting acoustic percussive attack
Keep your left-hand knuckles parallel to the fretboard to maintain rapid pull-off speed without touching adjacent strings
Do not rush the transition out of the intro—give the final E7 arpeggio full dramatic space before the electric guitars explode

techniques.name: Aeolian Power Chord Chugging & Expressive Pentatonic Bending
techniques.description: Locking into the driving 130 BPM rock groove with palm-muted downstroke power chords (A5 - G5 - F5 - G5), punctuated by Roger Fisher's biting blues-rock double-stops and full-step bends

notes: Chugging pulse: Crisp palm muting on the open low A string alternating with fret-7/8 dyad accents
Chorus accents: Wide open power chords ringing across the 5th and 6th strings
Solo phrasing: Aggressive unison bends at the 8th and 10th frets of the B and high E strings
sequence: Lock into steady eighth-note downstrokes on the A5 power chord with palm muting
Open up the right-hand attack on the beat-4 syncopated stabs into G5 and F5
Execute whole-step bends in the 5th-position A minor pentatonic box with wide vibrato
Blend rhythm acoustic strumming with electric crunch in the verse arrangements
tips: Rest the heel of the picking hand lightly against the bridge saddles for immediate muting control
Reinforce full-step bends on the G and B strings with index and middle fingers behind the ring finger
Use the bridge pickup on your electric guitar to cut through the heavy acoustic rhythm layer

sections.name: Acoustic Intro Prelude ('Silver Wheels')
sections.description: Nancy Wilson's immortal acoustic intro, widely considered one of the greatest acoustic rock performances ever recorded.
notes: Lightning-fast 16th-note pull-offs between fret 1 and open B string
Hybrid pick-and-finger attack for crisp volume
Resonant open-string sustain throughout

sections.name: Electric Guitar Riff Explosion & Verse 1
sections.description: The explosive band entrance as the delicate acoustic prelude gives way to a crushing wall of electric guitars and driving drums.
notes: Heavy downstrokes with palm muting on open A string
Pungent power chord punches locking with kick drum
Clear dynamic contrast compared to the intro

sections.name: Driving Electric Chorus Riff & Vocal Climax
sections.description: The heavy rock chorus groove powered by driving power chords and Roger Fisher's searing Les Paul fills.
notes: Open strumming without muting to let chords bloom
Syncopated accents on beats 2 and 4
Supporting Ann Wilson's soaring vocal hook

sections.name: Verse 2 Dynamic Acoustic-Electric Interplay
sections.technique: Layered Acoustic Rhythm & Electric Lead Stabs
sections.description: Intricate multi-guitar texture with Nancy's acoustic strumming meshing tightly with Fisher's biting blues stabs.
notes: Keep acoustic strumming percussive and bright
Electric guitar fills fill the spaces between vocal phrases
Crisp articulation on chord transitions

sections.name: Searing Blues-Rock Guitar Solo (Roger Fisher)
sections.description: Roger Fisher's blisteringly aggressive electric guitar solo, channeling classic Gibson Les Paul overdrive, wide vibrato, and screaming bends.
notes: Full-step bends at the 7th and 8th frets
Vicious pick attack with aggressive tube compression
Singing vibrato on sustained notes

sections.name: Outro Flurry & Power Chord Cadence
sections.technique: Acoustic Rasgueado Strumming & Crushing Outro Chords
sections.description: The epic finale combining Nancy's relentless acoustic strumming with thunderous electric power chords and soaring vocal screams.
notes: Maximum right-hand strumming intensity
Final power chord ring-out with amp feedback
Triumphant minor rock resolution

guitar.recommended: Ovation Custom Legend / Guild D-55 Acoustic (Nancy Wilson) & 1968 Gibson Les Paul Custom (Roger Fisher)
guitar.pickup: Acoustic piezo/mic blend for high-transient punch; Gibson T-Top humbuckers for biting electric crunch

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 50-watt / Fender Twin Reverb cranked for clean acoustic headroom

effects.distortion: Cranked Marshall valve crunch boosted with an MXR Distortion+
effects.reverb: Bright studio plate reverb adding spacious acoustic shimmer
effects.other: Acoustic compression and subtle stereo flanging on select verse transitions

beginner.title: Aeolian Chords & Electric Power Grooves
steps: Learn the root-5 and root-6 power chords for A5, G5, and F5
Practice downstroke strumming locked to 130 BPM with a metronome
Master the chorus progression (F - G - Am) with smooth transitions

intermediate.title: Acoustic Prelude Pull-Off Flurry
steps: Practice the 16th-note pull-off pattern between fret 1 and open B string slowly at 80 BPM
Develop finger independence between fretting index finger and open-string pull-offs
Increase speed gradually while keeping pull-offs loud and even in volume

advanced.title: Virtuosic Prelude Performance & Electric Solos
steps: Perform Nancy Wilson's complete 'Silver Wheels' prelude at full 130 BPM tempo without stumbling
Execute Roger Fisher's high-register screaming blues bends and unison double stops
Combine acoustic dexterity with hard-rock swagger in a full band live performance

commonMistakes: Stumbling on the open B string pull-offs in the intro by letting the fretting finger mute adjacent strings
Rushing the tempo during the acoustic prelude before the drums enter
Playing the verse power chords with too much gain, losing the biting percussive definition
practiceRoutine: 15 minutes: Nancy Wilson's pull-off flurry with metronome starting at 80 BPM and working to 130 BPM
10 minutes: Palm-muted power chord transitions (A5 - G5 - F5 - G5) with heavy downstrokes
15 minutes: Roger Fisher solo bends and unison double-stop intonation drills
focusAreas: Acoustic pull-off clarity and volume consistency
Seamless transition from delicate acoustic intro to aggressive electric rock
Pitch precision on high-register solo bends
metronomeWork: Practice the intro pull-offs at 80, 100, 115, and finally 130 BPM
